words: ثُمَّ تَلِينُ جُلُودُهُمْ وَقُلُوبُهُمْ إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī explains their skin and hearts softening toward God's remembrance as softening toward God's promise.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: {ثم تلين جلودهم وقلوبهم إلى ذكر الله} أي: إلى وعد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the condition of one God guides; whoever is unlike this is among those God misguides, with no guide for the one He misleads.
rows.anchor: هذه صفة من هداه الله، ومن كان على خلاف ذلك فهو ممن أضله الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned is reproached with the punishment earned, unlike the person who comes safely on Judgment Day; Ibn Kathīr compares this with face-walking and fire references.
rows.anchor: ويقرع فيقال له ولأمثاله من الظالمين: {ذوقوا ما كنتم تكسبون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse states only one side of the comparison; the poet's line about seeking good leaves its opposite unstated, meaning good or evil.
rows.anchor: واكتفى في هذه الآية بأحد القسمين عن الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Past generations who denied the messengers were destroyed for their sins, with no protector from God.
rows.anchor: القرون الماضية المكذبة للرسل، أهلكهم الله بذنوبهم، وما كان لهم من الله من واق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God suffices the servant who worships Him and relies on Him.
rows.anchor: يعني أنه تعالى يكفي من عبده وتوكل عليه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some read the word in the plural, His servants, instead of His servant.
rows.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم: "عباده"

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said success belongs to one guided to Islam who has sufficient livelihood and is content with it; al-Tirmidhī graded the report ṣaḥīḥ.
rows.anchor: عن فضالة بن عبيد الأنصاري؛ أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists threaten the Messenger with the idols and deities they invoke besides God, out of ignorance and error.
rows.anchor: يعني: المشركين يخوفون الرسول ويتوعدونه بأصنامهم وآلهتهم التي يدعونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is invincible: one who relies on Him cannot be overpowered, while He takes vengeance on those who disbelieve, associate partners, and defy His Messenger.
rows.anchor: منيع الجناب لا يضام، من استند إلى جنابه ولجأ إلى بابه، فإنه العزيز الذي لا أعز منه، ولا أشد انتقاما منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In hardship a person humbly turns to God, but after receiving a favor may become arrogant and claim it came from his own merit and special standing with God.
rows.anchor: أنه في حال الضراء يضرع إلى الله، عز وجل، وينيب إليه ويدعوه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatādah glosses the boast as meaning the person received the favor because of good or merit he possesses.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: {على علم عندي} على خير عندي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The favor is a test of whether its recipient obeys or disobeys, notwithstanding God's prior knowledge of the outcome.
rows.anchor: أنعمنا عليه بهذه النعمة لنختبره فيما أنعمنا عليه، أيطيع أم يعصي؟ مع علمنا المتقدم بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many earlier peoples made the same boast; their assertion was false and their amassed gains could not save them.
rows.anchor: أي: فما صح قولهم ولا منعهم جمعهم وما كانوا يكسبون

words: وَسِيقَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ زُمَرًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wretched disbelievers are driven violently toward Hell with rebuke and threats, thirsty as they go; the author links this to the contrast with the gathered righteous.
rows.anchor: وإنما يساقون سوقا عنيفا بزجر وتهديد ووعيد

words: وَسِيقَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ زُمَرًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are deaf, dumb, and blind, and some walk on their faces, as described in another verse.
rows.anchor: وهم في تلك الحال صم وبكم وعمي، منهم من يمشي على وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell's gates open immediately upon the disbelievers' arrival so their punishment can begin without delay.
rows.anchor: بمجرد وصولهم إليها فتحت لهم أبوابها سريعا، لتعجل لهم العقوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers are Zabāniyah, harsh in character and powerful, and their questioning rebukes and humiliates the arrivals.
rows.anchor: من الزبانية -الذين هم غلاظ الأخلاق، شداد القوى على وجه التقريع والتوبيخ والتنكيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers were of the disbelievers' own kind, so they could speak with and learn from them; their recitation established proofs, and they warned them of this Day's meeting.
rows.anchor: أي: من جنسكم تتمكنون من مخاطبتهم والأخذ عنهم

words: قَالُوا۟ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِنْ حَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ ٱلْعَذَابِ عَلَى ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They admit the messengers came, but say punishment became due because they denied and opposed them, turning from truth to falsehood in the misery they deserved.
rows.anchor: ولكن كذبناهم وخالفناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is left without a named speaker because all who see and know their state bear witness that they deserve the punishment under God's just judgment.
rows.anchor: أي: كل من رآهم وعلم حالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They remain in Hell without escape; their awful destination is the result of worldly arrogance and refusal to follow the truth.
rows.anchor: ماكثين فيها لا خروج لكم منها، ولا زوال لكم عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh resolves to kill Moses, telling his people to let him do it and saying he does not care if Moses calls on his Lord; Ibn Kathīr calls this defiance and obstinacy.
rows.anchor: وهذا عزم من فرعون -لعنه الله- على قتل موسى، عليه السلام، أي: قال لقومه: دعوني حتى أقتل لكم هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh claims Moses will mislead the people, alter their customs and practices, or spread corruption; the irony prompts the proverb that Pharaoh has become a preacher.
rows.anchor: يخشى فرعون أن يضل موسى الناس ويغير رسومهم وعاداتهم

words: أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most readers use the conjunction and before the charge that Moses would cause corruption in the land.
rows.anchor: قرأ الأكثرون: "أن يبدل دينكم وأن يظهر في الأرض الفساد"

words: أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Other readers retain or before the allegation that Moses would cause corruption in the land.
rows.anchor: وقرأ آخرون: {أو أن يظهر في الأرض الفساد}

words: أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some readers pronounce the verb with a ḍamma on its initial letter.
rows.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم: "يظهر في الأرض الفساد" بالضم

words: إِنِّى عُذْتُ بِرَبِّى وَرَبِّكُم مِّن كُلِّ مُتَكَبِّرٍ لَّا يُؤْمِنُ بِيَوْمِ ٱلْحِسَابِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Moses heard Pharaoh's threat, he sought God's protection from Pharaoh and every arrogant criminal who rejects the Day of Reckoning.
rows.anchor: قال موسى: استجرت بالله وعذت به من شره وشر أمثاله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abū Mūsā reports that when the Prophet feared a people, he prayed for refuge from their evil and for God to repel them; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: جاء في الحديث عن أبي موسى، رضي الله عنه، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا خاف قوما

words: وَقَالَ رَجُلٌۭ مُّؤْمِنٌۭ مِّنْ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The well-known view is that the believing man was a Copt from Pharaoh's household.
rows.anchor: المشهور أن هذا الرجل المؤمن كان قبطيا من آل فرعون

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says the believing man was Pharaoh's cousin.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: كان ابن عم فرعون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unspecified view identifies the believing man as the person who escaped with Moses.
rows.anchor: ويقال: إنه الذي نجا مع موسى

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarīr preferred that the man was a Copt from Pharaoh's family and rejected the Israelite identification, since Pharaoh listened to him and stopped short of killing Moses.
rows.anchor: واختاره ابن جرير (2) ، ورد قول من ذهب إلى أنه كان إسرائيليا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says only this man, Pharaoh's wife, and the person who warned Moses that the chiefs planned to kill him believed among Pharaoh's household; Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted it via Ibn Jurayj.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج عن ابن عباس: لم يؤمن من آل فرعون سوى هذا الرجل وامرأة فرعون

words: أَتَقْتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّىَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man had concealed his faith from the Copts, then openly rebuked Pharaoh out of anger for God; the commentator calls this a just word before an unjust ruler, the greatest such word before Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: فأخذت الرجل غضبة لله عز وجل

words: أَتَقْتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّىَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr recounts that ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ strangled the praying Prophet at the Kaʿbah until Abū Bakr pulled him away and recited this verse; al-Bukhārī alone reports it from al-Awzāʿī, with Ibn Isḥāq also transmitting it.
rows.anchor: قلت لعبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص: أخبرني بأشد شيء مما صنعه المشركون برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: أَتَقْتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّىَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ recounts Quraysh grabbing the Prophet's clothes after he challenged their worship of their ancestors; Abū Bakr held and defended him while crying and reciting the verse through its end. Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmits it.
rows.anchor: عن عمرو بن العاص أنه سئل: ما أشد ما رأيت قريشا بلغوا من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: أَتَقْتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّىَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: Al-Nasāʾī also reports the account through ʿAbdah, transmitting it as a report from ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ.
rows.anchor: وهكذا رواه النسائي من حديث عبدة، فجعله من مسند عمرو بن العاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer reasons that Moses has brought proof, then argues that even if he is a liar, leaving him alone lets God punish him; if he is truthful, harming him risks some of the promised punishment, so restraint is prudent.
rows.anchor: فمن العقل والرأي التام والحزم أن تتركوه ونفسه، فلا تؤذوه، فإن يك كاذبا فإن الله سيجازيه على كذبه

words: وَإِن يَكُ صَادِقًۭا يُصِبْكُم بَعْضُ ٱلَّذِى يَعِدُكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer's plea for restraint resembles Moses asking Pharaoh's people for a truce and permission to preach; Moses says to leave him alone if they will not believe.
rows.anchor: عن موسى، عليه السلام، أنه طلب من فرعون وقومه الموادعة

words: أَتَقْتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّىَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet similarly asked Quraysh not to harm him and to preserve their kinship; Ibn Kathīr reads the request as enabling him to call people and connects it to the Hudaybiyyah truce and its clear victory.
rows.anchor: فلا تؤذوني وتتركوا بيني وبين الناس

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌۭ كَذَّابٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Moses were the liar they claim, his speech and actions would be plainly disordered; instead his course is sound, and God would not guide a profligate liar to such orderly conduct.
rows.anchor: وهذا نرى أمره سديدا ومنهجه مستقيما، ولو كان من المسرفين الكذابين لما هداه الله، وأرشده إلى ما ترون من انتظام أمره وفعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer urges gratitude for God's gift of kingship and power by believing His Messenger, and warns the people not to invite God's punishment by denying him.
rows.anchor: قد أنعم الله عليكم بهذا الملك والظهور في الأرض بالكلمة النافذة والجاه العريض، فراعوا هذه النعمة بشكر الله، وتصديق رسوله

words: فَمَن يَنصُرُنَا مِن بَأْسِ ٱللَّهِ إِن جَآءَنَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their armies and troops cannot ward off any of God's might if He intends harm for them.
rows.anchor: لا تغني عنكم هذه الجنود وهذه العساكر، ولا ترد عنا شيئا من بأس الله إن أرادنا بسوء

words: قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ مَآ أُرِيكُمْ إِلَّا مَآ أَرَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh claims to advise only what he would choose for himself, but Ibn Kathīr says he knew Moses was truthful, citing Pharaoh's admission that God sent the signs and the account that they inwardly knew the truth.
rows.anchor: وقد كذب فرعون، فإنه كان يتحقق صدق موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's claimed counsel is a lie: he betrayed God, the Messenger, and his subjects, deceiving them instead of advising them.
rows.anchor: كذب فيه وافترى، وخان الله ورسوله ورعيته، فغشهم وما نصحهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh also lies when he claims to guide them to the right path: his people followed him, but Scripture says his command was not rightly guided and that he led them astray.
rows.anchor: وقال تعالى: {وأضل فرعون قومه وما هدى}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says an imam who dies while deceiving his subjects will not smell Paradise, whose scent is found from a distance of five hundred years.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث: "ما من إمام يموت يوم يموت وهو غاش لرعيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weak are followers and the arrogant are leaders; followers ask them to bear a share of their punishment, but the leaders refuse because all are in Hell and God apportions punishment by each person's deserts.
rows.anchor: {فيقول الضعفاء} وهم: الأتباع {للذين استكبروا}

words: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ فِى ٱلنَّارِ لِخَزَنَةِ جَهَنَّمَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despairing that God will accept or hear them after His command to be despised in Hell and remain silent, the inmates ask the keepers, like doorkeepers, to seek one day's respite.
rows.anchor: لما علموا أن الله، سبحانه، لا يستجيب منهم ولا يستمع لدعائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers remind them that messengers established proof; after the inmates admit it, the keepers tell them to pray for themselves, refuse to help or seek their release, and say praying will not change anything.
rows.anchor: أي: أوما قامت عليكم الحجج في الدنيا على ألسنة الرسل؟

words: وَمَا دُعَٰٓؤُا۟ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' supplication is futile: it is not accepted or answered.
rows.anchor: إلا من ذهاب، لا يتقبل ولا يستجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rebukes the polytheists for worshipping rivals beside Him, since He alone created, controls, and measures everything and is Lord of all worlds.
rows.anchor: وهو الخالق لكل شيء، القاهر لكل شيء، المقدر لكل شيء

words: قُلْ أَئِنَّكُمْ لَتَكْفُرُونَ بِٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلْأَرْضَ فِى يَوْمَيْنِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passage details the six-day creation: Earth was created first as the foundation before Heaven, while its later dahw means bringing out water and pasture after Heaven was created.
rows.anchor: فذكر أنه خلق الأرض أولا لأنها كالأساس، والأصل أن يبدأ بالأساس، ثم بعده بالسقف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A man asked Ibn ʿAbbās about apparent tensions in verses on mutual questioning, concealing polytheism, the order of Earth's and Heaven's creation, and descriptions of God's attributes.
rows.anchor: وقال المنهال، عن سعيد بن جبير قال: قال رجل لابن عباس: إني أجد في القرآن أشياء تختلف علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The smoke is water vapor rising from the Earth as it was created.
rows.anchor: وهو: بخار الماء المتصاعد منه حين خلقت الأرض

words: فَقَالَ لَهَا وَلِلْأَرْضِ ٱئْتِيَا طَوْعًا أَوْ كَرْهًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commanded Heaven and Earth to obey His command and respond to His act, willingly or under compulsion.
rows.anchor: أي: استجيبا لأمري، وانفعلا لفعلي طائعتين أو مكرهتين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God commanded the skies to bring out the sun, moon, and stars and the Earth to open rivers and produce fruits; they answered obediently.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله [تعالى] (1) {فقال لها وللأرض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their response means they submit with all they contain, ready for the angels, humans, and jinn God intends to create; Ibn Jarīr preferred Ibn ʿAbbās's reported explanation.
rows.anchor: بل نستجيب لك مطيعين بما فينا، مما تريد خلقه من الملائكة والإنس والجن جميعا

rows.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
rows.claim: A view Ibn Jarīr quotes from an Arab grammarian treats the two as rational speakers by representing them as speaking.
rows.anchor: حكاه ابن جرير عن بعض أهل العربية قال: وقيل: تنزيلا لهن معاملة من يعقل بكلامهما

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unspecified view says the Earth speaker was the place of the Kaʿbah and the Heaven speaker was the corresponding place above it.
rows.anchor: وقيل (3) إن المتكلم من الأرض بذلك هو مكان الكعبة

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī says that if Heaven and Earth had refused God's command, He would have punished them with pain; Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted this.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري: لو أبيا عليه أمره لعذبهما عذابا يجدان ألمه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayrah attributes to the Prophet a creation sequence: soil Saturday, mountains Sunday, trees Monday, hardships Tuesday, light Wednesday, animals Thursday, and Adam late Friday; Muslim and al-Nasāʾī transmit it, though Ibn Kathīr calls it unusual among Ṣaḥīḥ reports.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: أخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيدي فقال: "خلق الله التربة يوم السبت، وخلق فيها الجبال يوم الأحد

rows.speaker: البخاري
rows.claim: Al-Bukhārī criticizes the report's attribution to the Prophet, saying the more accurate version has Abū Hurayrah transmit it from Kaʿb al-Aḥbār.
rows.anchor: وقد علله البخاري في التاريخ فقال: رواه بعضهم عن أبي هريرة [رضي الله عنه] (3) عن كعب الأحبار، وهو الأصح
